tasks.short: Ask the patient's name and date of birth, verify them against the lab order and wristband or ID, find the order, and call the ward when details do not match.

steps.what: Phlebotomist asks the patient to state name and date of birth
Phlebotomist looks up the lab order by the patient's name
Phlebotomist verifies the patient's personal information against the lab order and wristband or ID
Phlebotomist calls the requesting ward when details do not match

tasks.design: The phlebotomist scans the barcode on the patient's wristband or appointment card with a handheld linked to the lab order system ({OTHER}), which opens the open orders and shows a match or mismatch. The patient still states name and date of birth aloud, and mismatches still go to the ward by phone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were found by typing names, and details compared by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Handhelds scan wristbands and cards and match them to open lab orders.
tasks.still_hard: Outpatients without a card or wristband still need a name search.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a confused patient answering to the wrong name.

reach.learn: Whether scan mismatches reveal wristband errors.

evidence.claim: Handheld scanners match wristband or card barcodes to open lab orders.
Health data are special category data; care use rests on Article 9(2)(h) with professional secrecy.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient at the booth to a confirmed identity; drawing blood is outside.
Input contract: lab orders from the requesting doctor in the order system; wristbands printed at admission; fallback is a name search.
The spoken identity check does not change.

incremental.description: Phlebotomist reports unreadable wristbands to the ward.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many outpatients without cards; high: most patients carry wristbands or cards.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Type patient details from paper request forms, enter tests and specimens and print labels, enter insurance details, check the entries, enter billing codes and fix entries the lab rejects.

steps.what: Phlebotomist types patient details from the paper request form
Phlebotomist enters tests and specimen details and prints labels
Phlebotomist enters insurance information
Phlebotomist checks entries against the request form
Phlebotomist enters billing codes for the collection
Phlebotomist fixes entries the lab rejects

tasks.design: Electronic lab orders from GPs and wards arrive in the lab order system ({OTHER}) with patient, tests and tube types, so scanning the order prints the labels. Insurance details are checked against the national insurance check, and billing codes follow from the order and the confirmed collection once the phlebotomist has checked the entry. Paper forms that still arrive are typed in; checking stays with the phlebotomist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper request forms were typed in, and insurance and billing details entered by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic ordering links GP and ward systems to the lab, and insurance details can be checked automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Some GPs still send paper forms.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a requested tube type cannot be right for the test.
tasks.altitude: The phlebotomist checks entries instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: Lab orders and specimen labels can come straight from the order system instead of being retyped.
The medical dossier is kept 20 years from the last change and shared only with consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the request form to corrected entries; payment is outside.
Input contract: electronic orders from GPs and wards; insurance check from the national service; tariffs set by lab finance; fallback is typing from paper.
GPs' ordering time does not change.
unknowns: Share of orders still on paper.

incremental.description: Phlebotomist scans paper forms the order system cannot read.

approvals.approved_version: The entry as checked by the phlebotomist in s4; a corrected entry needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many GPs still send paper forms; high: most orders arrive electronically.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check results are complete and authorised, phone critical results to the physician, send routine results, answer physicians' questions about results and sample quality, and log that results were given.

steps.what: Phlebotomist checks that sample analysis results are complete and authorised by the lab
Phlebotomist phones critical results to physicians with read-back
Phlebotomist faxes or posts routine results to GPs
Phlebotomist answers physicians' questions about results and sample quality
Phlebotomist logs which results were given to whom

tasks.design: The lab system ({OTHER}) shows which results are authorised and complete. Routine results go to the GP's system as electronic messages once checked, and each message is logged by the system. Critical results are still phoned with read-back, and the phlebotomist records the call in a short form. Answering physicians' questions stays with the phlebotomist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routine results went by fax or post and every result given was logged by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Lab systems send results to GP systems as electronic messages and log them.
tasks.still_hard: Critical results must reach a person, not an inbox.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining that a high potassium may come from a difficult draw.

reach.learn: Whether electronic results reach the GP faster.

evidence.claim: Lab systems can send results to GP systems as electronic messages and log each one.
The medical dossier is shared only with consent, with an access log on request.

assumptions: Boundary: from authorised results to the results log; interpretation by the physician is outside.
Input contract: results authorised by the lab specialist; GP addresses from the order; fallback is fax and post.
Phoning critical results and answering questions do not change.
GPs' time is outside the phlebotomist's savings.
unknowns: Share of GPs receiving electronic results.

incremental.description: Phlebotomist resends results that fail to deliver.

approvals.approved_version: The results as authorised by the lab and checked complete by the phlebotomist in s1.
The results as authorised by the lab and checked complete by the phlebotomist in s1.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many GPs still on fax; high: most GPs take electronic results.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Label tubes and note collection times, fill in the courier's transport list, record the hand-over, check arrival and chase missing samples, and log sample problems.

steps.what: Phlebotomist labels tubes and writes the collection time on the request form
Phlebotomist fills in the transport list for the courier
Phlebotomist documents the route of specimens at hand-over to the courier
Phlebotomist checks arrival at the lab and chases missing samples
Phlebotomist records sample problems such as haemolysis or the wrong tube

tasks.design: Labels print at the collection point from the order with the collection time on scan. Tubes are scanned into the transport box, which builds the transport list, and a scan at hand-over and at lab arrival tracks each sample in the lab system ({OTHER}). A view lists samples not yet arrived, and sample problems are logged with a reason code.
tasks.previous_blocker: Times, transport lists and hand-overs were written on paper, and missing samples found by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Barcode scanning at each hand-over tracks samples from collection to lab.
tasks.still_hard: Samples from home visits travel outside the scanned route.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which courier run a late sample probably missed.

reach.learn: Whether scanned hand-overs cut lost samples.

evidence.claim: Barcode scans at collection, hand-over and lab arrival can track each sample in the lab system.
Health data are special category data; care use rests on Article 9(2)(h).

assumptions: Boundary: from collected samples to the sample incident log; analysis is outside.
Input contract: orders and tube types from the lab order system; courier runs set by the lab; fallback is paper lists.
Couriers scan boxes instead of signing paper lists; about the same time.
Logging problems stays with the phlebotomist.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many home-visit samples outside the scanned route; high: all samples collected at scanned points.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The phlebotomist keeps identity checks, critical calls and judging sample problems; typing forms, paper lists and faxes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A phlebotomist whose time goes to patients, not paperwork.
